findings.summary: JACK Audio Connection Kit is a professional sound server API and daemon pair providing real-time, low-latency connections for audio and MIDI data between applications on Unix-like systems. It serves as the de facto standard for professional audio software on Linux since 2002. Two implementations exist: jack1 in plain C and jack2 in C++ with multi-processor scalability and cross-platform support. JACK can use various hardware back-ends and provides a backwards-compatible API layer for PipeWire. Its low-latency performance drove real-time kernel optimizations in the Linux 2.6 series.

mechanisms.title: Real-time audio and MIDI routing
mechanisms.explanation: JACK functions as an API and daemon pair that establishes real-time, low-latency connections for audio and MIDI data between applications, operating as a professional sound server.

mechanisms.title: Scheduling and kernel optimization
mechanisms.explanation: JACK's low-latency scheduling requirements were a driving force behind real-time optimization efforts for the Linux kernel 2.6 series, including the -rt branch and PREEMPT_RT patch to improve audio performance.
